findings.reads: body: "Real estate can be deeded to and held by a protected series in its own name. Under §605.2301, the recorded deed stands as the record that the property belongs to that series.",
findings.claims: That under §605.2301 a recorded deed is, without qualification, the record that the property belongs to the series.

Batch 17 (Ruling 14; docs/facts.md:212 "The recorded-real-property-instrument exception has the giving-value and lack-of-knowledge qualifications stated in s.605.2301(2)(b)") rewrote The Statute page (TheStatute.tsx:59) to carry those conditions; this card, shown on the Home and Benefits pages, still states the unconditional version.
findings.replacement: body: "Real estate can be deeded to and held by a protected series in its own name. findings.where: Order form, Certification step on the adding-series path, the opening paragraph
findings.reads: Florida establishes a protected series when the company files a
findings.claims: A protected series exists as of the filing of its Designation.
findings.truth: The 2026 s. 605.2201(3) (Online Sunshine, opened 20 Sep 2026): 'A protected series is established when the protected series designation takes effect under s. 605.0207' — a Designation may carry a delayed effective date, and s. 605.2201(2) requires it to be 'signed by the company'. The sentence is right about consent (s. 605.2201(1)) but places establishment at filing rather than at the effective date.
findings.replacement: Florida establishes a protected series when a Protected Series Designation, signed for the company and filed with the Division of Corporations with the consent of all of its members, takes effect (§605.2201). There are no Articles to sign: your company already exists.

findings.where: FAQ page, question 10 "Does this work for out-of-state investors?", the sentence citing §605.0905(3)
findings.reads: a: "A Florida Protected Series LLC works well for Floridians and for Florida businesses and assets. There is no way to guarantee how the courts of another state — particularly one with no series LLC legislation of its own — will interpret it. There is also a registration question that runs in both directions: under §605.0905(3), owning income-producing real property or tangible personal property in a state is itself transacting business there, which means a company formed elsewhere that owns Florida rental property has to qualify here — and a Florida company that buys rental property in another state should expect that state to take the same position. The consequences of skipping it are real: §605.0904 bars a company transacting business in Florida without a certificate of authority from maintaining an action here, and §605.0904(7) adds liability for all back fees plus a civil penalty of at least $500 and not more than $1,000 for each year or part of a year. If you are not a Floridian, or you plan to hold out-of-state property in a Florida Protected Series LLC, you should seek advice from an attorney licensed to practice in the relevant state.",
findings.claims: That §605.0905(3) makes owning income-producing real or tangible personal property "in a state" transacting business "there" — a rule stated for any state.
findings.truth: s. 605.0905(3) (2026 Florida Statutes, opened on Online Sunshine) reads "The ownership in this state of income-producing real property or tangible personal property, other than property excluded under subsection (1), constitutes transacting business in this state for purposes of s. 605.0902(1)." It speaks only of Florida. The answer's second half (another state "should expect … the same position") is a prediction about other states' law, which the Florida section does not support; the citation should carry only the Florida rule.
findings.replacement: There is also a registration question that runs in both directions: under §605.0905(3), owning income-producing real property or tangible personal property in Florida is itself transacting business here, which means a company formed elsewhere that owns Florida rental property has to qualify here — and a Florida company that buys rental property in another state should expect that state to apply its own version of the same rule.

findings.where: Operating agreement masters, statement-of-authority section (s. 5.9 member-managed multi; s. 5.7 member-managed single; s. 5.8 manager-managed forms) — all eight masters
findings.reads: **5.9 Statement of Authority.** With the consent of all Members required by Section 5.5(i), the Members may cause the Company to file with the Department a statement of authority under s. 605.0302, Florida Statutes, stating the authority, or the limitations on the authority, of Members to transfer or encumber real property held in the name of the Company or of a Protected Series, and may cause a certified copy of that statement to be recorded in the official records of any county in which the real property is located. A statement so filed shall be consistent with this Agreement, and the Members shall cause it to be amended or cancelled as necessary to keep it accurate. The limitations in Section 5.4(b) apply among the Members whether or not a statement of authority is filed or recorded.
findings.claims: The Company may file a s. 605.0302 statement of authority stating the authority or limitations on authority to transfer or encumber real property 'held in the name of the Company or of a Protected Series'.
findings.truth: s. 605.0302(1)(b)-(c) and (7) address 'real property held in the name of the company' / 'held in the name of a limited liability company'; the section never mentions a protected series. A protected series is 'a person distinct from' the company (s. 605.2103), and s. 605.0302 reaches it only through s. 605.2108(3) ('the provisions of this chapter applicable to limited liability companies in general … are applicable … to each protected series'), under which the protected series would file its own statement for property held in its name. Same text in templates-oa-member-s.md:200, templates-oa-member-single-s.md:154, templates-oa-member-single.md:148, templates-oa-multi.md:194, templates-oa-s.md:194, templates-oa-single-s.md:168, templates-oa-single.md:162. Evidence: evidence/statutes/605.0302.txt, 605.2103.txt, 605.2108.txt.
findings.replacement: In each master, after 'held in the name of the Company or of a Protected Series,' add: 'and, as to real property held in the name of a Protected Series, may cause that Protected Series to file its own statement of authority under s. 605.0302 as applied by s. 605.2108(3), Florida Statutes,' (Adam to confirm the drafting).
